gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the wireless under-$50 boards' maker-stated battery capacities side by side: ATK states 12,000 mAh for the A87 at $29.98, Royal Kludge states 1,450 mAh for the RK61 at $49.99, and none of the four rival pages read mentions the A87 at all.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com (cited), rottenwifi.com (cited), official.deals/under-50 and mechvibes.com. None has a battery or polling-rate column, none gives battery hours, and none lists the ATK A87, Rosewill Neon S75, DAREU FLEX75 or Redragon K526 Pro. Rottenwifi and Mechvibes already state the RK61's 1,450 mAh, and ChatGPT's own answer already shows 12,000 mAh for the A87, so the new part is only the side-by-side with prices read today. The table is also incomplete: Shopify returned HTTP 429 on the Gamakay, ATK and Redragon product pages, so battery mAh for our two Gamakay rows, battery hours and polling rate per connection mode are all missing. With those rows filled this could reach 2.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's overall pick rather than changing it: the ATK A87 has the largest maker-stated battery read (about 8.3 times the RK61's) at the lowest price read, $29.98 at atk.store against the $34.98 ChatGPT showed. It is not ours. Our Gamakay TK101 at $47.99 does not win on battery; it honestly wins only the number-pad segment, as the one 98% (101-key) tri-mode board in the set. The Gamakay NS68 tri-mode at $39.99 fits as the Hall effect option. Two footnotes change which variant to quote: Redragon's K530 Pro is $49.99 only in the two white variants (the black red, blue and brown variants are $54.99, over budget), and Royal Kludge's $49.99 RK61 is the single-colour-backlit version (the Color-Block Edition is $59.99, over budget).
